instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company runs an Amazon ECS service on AWS Fargate in private subnets. Stringent security rules forbid any route from these subnets to the internet, and the security team reviews every resource that the company adds to the VPC. An internal Application Load Balancer must send requests to the tasks, and the tasks must pull their container image privately from Amazon ECR. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on public IP address assignment for the tasks, so that the tasks reach Amazon ECR without a route to an internet gateway.

options.label: B
options.text: Create the target group of the load balancer with the instance target type, and attach the target group to the ECS service.

options.label: C
options.text: Create interface VPC endpoints for every AWS service that offers them in the Region, and create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3.

options.label: D
options.text: Create interface VPC endpoints for the Amazon ECR API and the Docker registry, and create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3.

options.label: E
options.text: Create the target group of the load balancer with the ip target type, and attach the target group to the ECS service.

items.stem: A company runs an Amazon ECS service on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The group has sufficient instances for the day peak. At night, service auto scaling lowers the task count, but the number of instances stays the same, and most instances run few tasks. The company wants to stop paying for idle instances at night. Which combination of steps is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Change the task placement strategy of the service to spread on instance ID, so that each instance runs a share of the tasks.

options.label: B
options.text: Add an Auto Scaling group capacity provider with managed scaling to the capacity provider strategy of the service, with a target capacity of 100 percent.

options.label: C
options.text: Lower the minimum task count of the service auto scaling policy, so that service auto scaling also removes the idle instances.

options.label: D
options.text: Change the task placement strategy of the service to binpack on memory, so that the tasks fill as few instances as possible.

options.label: E
options.text: Add an Auto Scaling group capacity provider with managed scaling to the capacity provider strategy of the service, with a target capacity of 50 percent to keep spare instances.
